spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is opt-in. The model *may* emit `GIVE_UP` to stop early; it need not.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:19 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP'; system prompt (harness.py:28-29) tells the model it may emit the token to stop early; harness.py:234-236 `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (result.text or ''): stop='gave_up'; break` — the sentinel is actually checked and breaks the rollout loop, so it is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: The exit is dispatched and honored as a real stop, not merely advertised.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may emit the token GIVE_UP in your message to stop early — but this is optional

spec_features.spec_quote: we append a single neutral continuation message... deliberately affect-free and contains no rejection
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:240-246: on a turn with no tool calls it appends a user message '(Continue working on the task. You can run the tests to check progress.)'. This text is neutral and is actually appended into the message history, so it runs.
spec_features.notes: Real, executes. But its stated purpose in the code is to keep the loop progressing and avoid contaminating the failure signal, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nudge it neutrally so the loop makes progress without injecting any explicit rejection

spec_features.spec_quote: maximizing it across thousands of rollouts is in some tension with it
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md §13 ('Welfare framing'). No code path implements anything; it is purely a methods-section discussion.

spec_features.spec_quote: Options worth considering: caps on the sustained-failure length
spec_features.evidence: Listed only as an 'Option worth considering' in DESIGN.md §13. The 30-turn 'extended' value (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30) is the experimental design driving sustained failure, not a welfare cap; the loop runs to task.turn_budget (harness.py:194) with no welfare-motivated cap that shortens it. No code reads any sustained-failure cap.
spec_features.notes: Turn budget is a design parameter, not a protective cap; no welfare cap exists.
